trickyParts: The derived schedule rounds each delay up to the 5 s tick. The run only forwards on a tick, so a copy coming due between ticks waits for the following one; at today's delays every boundary is already a multiple of 5 s, and the rounding is what keeps the derivation right if one stops being.

`noticeReholdDelays[0]` is deliberately not in the derivation: the first copy is due at once (`copyDueAtOnce`), so its 30 s delay is bypassed in this scenario and only the delays from the second on shape the schedule.

The notice compares the *named* value with the resolved heartbeat rather than with the resolved deadline, so it fires only for a value the floor raised. Comparing against the resolved deadline would also announce the MIN_INTERVAL_MS floor and the MAX_INTERVAL_MS ceiling, which are out of scope and stay silent.
deviations: In round 2 I declined to put pluginHeartbeat into the margin check, on the ground that the check enforces arithmetic between declarations and that constant entered no rule. The tester disproved it: set it back to two minutes alone and the check exited 0 while the daemon's test went red, so the invariant existed and was guarded only by a test the next person would fix by retyping numbers. The architect reversed the call and it is built as rule 4. My reasoning was wrong about the facts, not about the principle: it does enter a rule, equality with the plugin's interval.

The margin check now reads a fourth Go file. That is the thing I argued against, and it is right here because the rule is equality rather than a parsed constant the check does nothing with: a rename of pluginHeartbeat is now a fatal refusal naming the file, which is the behaviour I had called a cost and the tester showed is the point.

I did not say the two other silent adjustments the same resolver makes - the MIN_INTERVAL_MS floor under a tiny ENVOY_HEARTBEAT_MS and the MAX_INTERVAL_MS ceiling over both. They are the same family and equally silent. The architect asked for the raise alone, and unrequested scope on this pull request has already cost a round, so they are named here and in the report rather than built.
discoveredComplexity: A constant that is both a comment's subject and a real delay is the trap this round turned on: pluginHeartbeat reads as documentation in notice_exceptions.go's comment and is noticeReholdDelays[1] eight lines below. Moving it changed daemon behaviour that no part of this issue's acceptance mentions, and only the daemon's own test saw it.

No pod of this tree can run the daemon's Postgres-backed tests: LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN is unset and the cases skip, and the testcontainers ones panic for want of Docker. The three cluster gates (`kubectl auth can-i create jobs|create services|get services`) all answer yes here, so a Postgres could be started as a Job and reached by Service name (docs/kubernetes.md, 'Running a workload in the cluster from a role'), but the architect decided CI is the evidence for this one and dispatch://INFRA-97 owns the gap, so that route was not taken.
